# Nvidia giver afkast på 65 pct. årligt - kan opturen fortsætte?

**Feed**: borsen-podcast  
**Published**: 2026-09-02  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

This Danish market podcast (Børsen) covers the ongoing AI investment boom with Nvidia framed as 'the world's most important stock' — trading at a PE ~24 that panelists call not-cheap-but-not-expensive, while flagging rising competition (Qualcomm, Google TPUs), datacenter monetization doubts and its huge size as risks. Guests Lars Hytting (Artoscope) and Kurt Kara (MyInvest) are broadly constructive on strong Danish large-caps after a strong earnings season, but warn on rising G7 rates ('financial repression') and high-multiple growth stocks; Meta is cited as a favourite cheap AI beneficiary. A 'top three' segment covers chronically underperforming Danish icons — Tivoli, Bang & Olufsen and Harboe — all viewed skeptically.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 META — Meta | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 75%

Kurt (MyInvest guest) holds it: very cheap on lawsuit overhang nearing resolution, 28% ad-revenue growth driven by AI, clear AI beneficiary.

#### Reasoning

Guest Kurt Kara argues Meta is a prime AI beneficiary (like banks/Netflix/Apple were in the internet era rather than the pick-shovel makers), trading cheaply because near-resolved lawsuits depress the multiple, while AI-driven advertising lifted revenue 28% YoY. He owns it as part of a diversified portfolio.

#### Sell Triggers

- if lawsuits resolve unfavorably
- if AI-driven ad revenue growth decelerates
- if datacenter capex fails to generate returns

> *"Vi har för exempel Meta, och det är för att den är otroligt billig på grund av alla de rättssägar som vi menar nog ska löses... genom att använda AI har de fått 28% framgång i reklamintäkterna över ett år."*

---

### 🟡 GN — GN Store Nord | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Lars holds it in the all-star portfolio; a patience case awaiting the hearing-aid transaction to close, after which GN gets cash to buy back shares; expects it among best performers rest of year.

#### Reasoning

Lars (Artoscope) frames GN as a patience/turnaround case held ~4 years with no return; 2026 is a 'transport year' pending a hearing transaction. Once closed, GN gets substantial cash for buybacks and operational focus should improve the stock; he retains full confidence and bought the new headset himself.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the hearing transaction fails to close
- if a new capital raise is needed
- if operational drift continues after the deal

> *"Jag förväntar mig att GN vill vara bland de bäst performande resten av året... Så snart den gör det så får GN massor av pengar i lommarna. Och kan börja strax få aktier tillbaka i köp."*

---

### 🟡 DEMANT — Demant | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Cleaned up before earnings, delivered results and is building a new product platform; Lars is up ~30% (+17,300 kr) on it in the all-star portfolio.

#### Reasoning

Lars cites Demant as a positive earnings-season standout that tidied up before its report, delivered on guidance and is forging a new product platform. It has been his best all-star portfolio contributor (~+30%), supporting continued conviction.

#### Sell Triggers

- if new product platform underdelivers
- if next quarterly guidance disappoints

> *"Vi kan heller inte komma ut med Demant. Som alldeles var städat rätt fint upp till sin regnskapsavläggelse. Och alldeles bara levererar varan och smider en ny produktplattform på."*

---

### 🟡 NVDA — Nvidia | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 55%

World's most important AI stock, doubled revenue, PE ~24 seen as not expensive; but panelists warn of intensifying competition, datacenter monetization doubts, power costs and its huge size.

#### Reasoning

Panel consensus: keep riding the AI wave via the leading tech (Jesper), and the valuation isn't stretched (PE ~24, ~10 in two years). But Kurt and Lars flag that extraordinary earnings are a 'window' that competition (Qualcomm, Google TPUs) will normalize, datacenter ROI is uncertain pressuring margins, and 83/80 analyst buys signal crowded consensus — a reason for caution, not fresh buying.

#### Sell Triggers

- if AI datacenter capex proves unprofitable
- if competitors (Qualcomm/Google TPU) erode chip pricing
- if the AI investment bubble deflates
- if gross margins compress

> *"Jag är enig. Jag vill inte säga att den är billig, men den ser inte dyr ut... men man ska bara huska... när historien är fantastisk och prisen också är tillsvarande. Det kan vara en giftig cocktail."*

---

### ⛔ BO — Bang & Olufsen | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Down 87% from peak, 1.6% avg annual return over 35y; some comeback signs (stronger operational footing per Danske Bank) but falling revenue; Kurt skeptical long-term, only a possible 'cigar butt' bounce.

#### Reasoning

Kurt calls B&O 'the cat with nine lives' repeatedly bailed out by cheap capital raises; its old high-margin design-TV model was broken by flatscreens, and the pivot to sound is a poor fit because sound isn't visible design. Falling revenue remains unsolved. At best a short-term 'cigar butt' bounce, not a long-term hold.

#### Sell Triggers

- if another dilutive capital raise is announced
- if revenue keeps declining
- if audio pivot fails to gain traction

> *"Därför tror jag inte på den på den långa banan. Men det kan säkert vara att den kommer så långt ner att man får ett lyft. Och det är det som i vår investeringsvärld heter ett cigarettskåd."*

---

### ⛔ HARB-B — Harboe | **AVOID** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

0.89% avg annual return over 35y; heavy shareholder criticism, family holds voting majority with small equity stake, poor capital allocation and crowded beer market.

#### Reasoning

Both guests decline to invest: Kurt won't touch a company where management/family has full control via voting majority but not aligned capital, combined with poor capital allocation and a commoditized, oversupplied beer market. Lars similarly cites lack of trust in the leadership.

#### Sell Triggers

- N/A — thesis is to avoid; would reconsider only on governance overhaul or aligned family ownership

> *"Jag vill inte röra det här i alla fall. Jag har aldrig gjort det och kommer heller inte till det... Under normala omständigheter vill jag också avstå från att investera i sällskapar där ledelsen ejer en minoritet men har fullkommen kontroll."*

---

### ⛔ TIV — Tivoli | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 55%

3% avg annual return over 35y, big underperformance; plans to invest up to ~1bn kr in the park with little left for shareholders; hard to see the catalyst.

#### Reasoning

Neither guest owns it. Jens Løstrup (cited) avoids companies that invest so heavily in themselves that nothing returns to shareholders — the core issue here. With capital ploughed into the park and only vague plans for more guests/rides, the value-unlock catalyst is unclear.

#### Sell Triggers

- if heavy self-investment continues to crowd out shareholder returns
- if visitor growth stalls

> *"Något av det han säger är att han helst aldrig vill investera i ett sällskap som investerar så tungt själv att det inte är något tillbaka till aktionärerna. Och det är lite det som är utfordringen i den här casen."*

---

### 🟡 NOVO-B — Novo Nordisk | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 45%

Used as cautionary tale: was Europe's largest firm, fell ~70%+ from top as GLP-1 monopoly eroded by competitors (Eli Lilly, others); worst all-star contributor this week.

#### Reasoning

Kurt invokes Novo to show that even the largest, best-story stocks can fall 70-75%, as its GLP-1 exclusivity gave way to a 'forest of producers'. It is the worst weekly contributor in the all-star portfolio (-1700 kr) and Johnny's portfolio holding Novo/DSV lost 12,000 kr — signalling caution rather than conviction either way.

#### Sell Triggers

- if GLP-1 competition further compresses pricing/share
- if growth rates keep decelerating from prior ~100%+ levels

> *"Novo Nordisk var faktiskt Europas största sällskap. Och fallt 70% från toppen, om inte mer... när stort sett alla råber köp... är det grund till att bli skeptisk."*

---

### 🟠 JYSK — Jyske Bank | **WATCH** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 55%

Breaking acquisition of Formuepleje sent stock to all-time high (~1100); ~200m kr/yr expected commission income, guidance unchanged; undisclosed price flagged, question whether deal reenergizes the stock.

#### Reasoning

Simon reports the surprise Formuepleje acquisition drove Jyske Bank to record highs; major shareholder Jens Løstrup was first excited then cautious given the undisclosed price. The open question is whether the deal restarts the share price — a watch item pending disclosed terms and integration.

#### Sell Triggers

- if acquisition price is revealed as overpaid
- if commission income undershoots the ~200m kr/yr estimate
- if integration disappoints

> *"Det sänder ju Jyske Bank-aktien upp i högsta kurs någonsin idag... Så må vi se om det är det som kan ge Jyske Bank-aktien något förnyet energi och något genstart av aktiekassan där."*

---
